lore:
*Goblinus Malictus*, commonly termed the Goblin, is the persistent shadow upon the fringes of our maps. These diminutive humanoids thrive in the lightless damp of limestone caverns and the sun-starved undergrowth of ancient briars. They are not merely beasts, but a collective blight of low cunning.

Their predation is defined by a cruel patience. Goblins eschew honorable combat, preferring the "thousand-cut" ambush. They utilize jagged scrap-metal and crude grease-traps to hobble the unwary, descending only when their quarry is spent. They possess a magpie’s hunger, often valuing a shiny thimble as highly as the meat of the kill.

In provincial folklore, the goblin is the "Thief of the Hearth." Villagers hang sprigs of rowan and cold iron charms to deter these "unbidden guests" from souring the cream or spiriting away silver spoons. To find a goblin’s track near one’s home is viewed as an omen of impending rot—a grim sign that the civil world is being slowly reclaimed by the chaotic, sniggering dark.
